presets.title: Aman then Boro rice rotation
presets.summary: Aman rice in the monsoon followed by Boro rice in the dry season fits this field, which has reliable irrigation and no standing water detected in recent monsoons. The two crops leave a short fallow between Boro harvest and Aman sowing, so the rotation is calendar-feasible if Aman is harvested on time.
reasons: Aman rice duration of about 135 days fits the Jun-Oct wet season, and Boro rice duration of about 150-160 days fits the Dec-May dry season with irrigation.
The field has reliable irrigation, which is essential for Boro rice in the cool dry Nov-Feb and hot pre-monsoon Mar-May periods.
Satellite check found no standing water near the field in the 2024-25 monsoons, reducing Aman flood risk compared with a chronically waterlogged field.
Aman to fallow to Boro is a listed rotation pattern in the Rangpur research data.
risks: Late Aman harvest would delay Boro transplanting and push Boro into hotter, drier conditions.
Boro rice depends entirely on reliable irrigation and timely water supply in the dry season.
Rice blast and other rice diseases can affect both seasons, especially with dense planting or excess nitrogen.
Aman remains exposed to monsoon flooding or waterlogging in an unusually wet year despite the recent clear satellite checks.
requirements: Maintain reliable irrigation for the full Boro season, including Mar-May.
Use varieties and transplanting dates that allow Aman harvest by November and Boro sowing in December.
Apply fertilizer according to soil test and the Fertilizer Recommendation Guide 2024, rather than blanket doses.
Monitor for rice blast and other diseases and use recommended resistant varieties and field sanitation.

Mungbean duration of 55-58 days fits a March sowing to May harvest in the hot pre-monsoon season, before monsoon waterlogging.

risks: Potato late blight and other diseases in cool humid spells, and tuber damage if harvest is delayed into wet weather.

Seed potato quality and storage, and mungbean seed quality, affect yield and disease.

requirements: Use certified or well-selected seed potato and timely planting in November, with good drainage and earthing up.
Sow mungbean promptly after potato harvest in late February to March and harvest before monsoon rains.
Use soil-test based fertilizer following the Fertilizer Recommendation Guide 2024, rather than blanket doses.
Keep monsoon fallow or use it only for drainage maintenance and green manure, not for these two crops.

presets.title: Aman-Boro double rice rotation
presets.summary: Aman rice in the monsoon followed by Boro rice in the dry season fits this field and the reliable irrigation available. This is a recognised Aman-fallow-Boro rotation for Rangpur, with a short fallow and land preparation between harvests. It needs timely sowing, irrigation for Boro, and disease and nutrient management, but no fundamental climate or waterlogging barrier was found.
reasons: Aman rice uses monsoon rainfall and suits the Jun-Oct wet season, while Boro rice uses the cool dry Nov-Apr season with reliable irrigation.
The field check found no standing water near the field in the 2024-25 monsoons, so Aman is not ruled out by chronic flooding, though monsoon water management is still needed.
Clay loam soil can hold water for rice, and pH 5.85 is workable with appropriate fertiliser and, if advised locally, liming.
Aman (about 135 days) and Boro (about 150-160 days) durations fit a one-year rotation with a May fallow for land preparation.
risks: Boro depends entirely on reliable irrigation and timely water in the dry season; any irrigation failure will cut yield.
Rice blast and other diseases can affect both seasons, especially with dense planting, excess nitrogen, and humid weather.
Acidic soil at pH 5.85 may limit nutrient availability without soil-test-based fertiliser and possible liming.
Double rice removes nutrients twice a year and can degrade soil structure and organic matter if residues are removed and no fallow management is used.
requirements: Use a locally recommended Aman variety for monsoon sowing in June and a Boro variety sown in late November to December.
Ensure irrigation water, pump/fuel, and labour are secured before sowing Boro, and maintain shallow standing water for Aman without deep flooding.
Follow Fertilizer Recommendation Guide 2024 and local soil-test advice for fertiliser and liming; do not apply blanket high nitrogen.
Scout weekly for blast and other rice diseases and use only locally approved control measures at label rates.
Use the May fallow to clear residues, repair bunds and drains, and prepare land for Aman.
